gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured figure for how much a two-screen extender dims when the laptop alone powers it: Notebookcheck measured the Uperfect Delta's two 15.6-inch screens at 160 cd/m² on one USB-C cable and 226 cd/m² with the included 30 W adapter, and Expert Reviews found the ASUS ZenScreen Duo OLED went into a reboot loop when brightness was set much above about 50% on one cable.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited and against the uncited top results. Xebec's comparison page and its Tri-Screen 3 page give no brightness or power figures. Macworld's best-portable-monitors list (Simon Jary, 2026-10-16) prints maker specs such as 300 nits and 100% sRGB for the Trio 3 Pro, never says which figures are measured, and does not cover the ZenScreen Duo or Uperfect Delta. itechguides' list of 15 says only in general terms that laptop power 'may reduce brightness or stability' and has no number or named tester. deskgearhq states that 'independent third-party lab testing of these exact ASINs is limited' and lists only maker claims. Tom's Hardware's list did not load past the site navigation. Dealectric's own page already carries Macworld's note that the Trio 3 Pro is below full brightness on laptop power, but it has no measured nit figures. So rivals have the idea in qualitative form, and a measured before-and-after figure from a named lab is new.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. A day trader keeps the screens lit for a whole session, so every two-screen extender should be planned with a power adapter plugged in. Notebookcheck's figures (a 29% drop from 226 to 160 cd/m² on laptop power, measured on the Uperfect Delta that ChatGPT recommended as its #3) and Macworld's finding on the Trio 3 Pro say to budget for wall power. Neither tells a buyer to switch screens. No named lab has published measured brightness or colour for the Trio 3 Pro, Xebec Tri-Screen 3, Duex Float 2 Pro or the FOPO S-series, so those rows can carry only maker specs. On measurements alone, no candidate beats another.
candidates: FOPO S11 / S10 / S7 dual extenders

findings.label: Measured max brightness on laptop USB-C power vs with power adapter
findings.value: 160 cd/m² on a single USB-C cable; 226 cd/m² with the included PD 30 W adapter
findings.source_title: Uperfect UStation Delta review: Portable monitor with dual 15.6-inch displays expands the desktop (Notebookcheck, Sebastian Bade, 2023-08-20)
findings.note: Measured with an X-Rite i1Pro 2. Notebookcheck notes the unit was a prototype. The loss works out to 226 − 160 = 66 cd/m², or 29%. Notebookcheck says one cable runs both screens but does not say how (DisplayLink, MST or Alt Mode).

findings.label: Measured average brightness, contrast, sRGB coverage and colour error
findings.value: 200 cd/m² average across both screens; contrast 471:1 (upper screen) and 1,026:1 (lower screen); 73.3% sRGB; ColorChecker ΔE2000 6.64 as shipped, 3.53 after calibration
findings.note: Instruments: X-Rite i1Pro 2, Argyll 3D for gamut coverage, CalMAN for ΔE. No PWM flicker at any brightness. It is not confirmed that this is the exact listing ChatGPT showed as 'UPERFECT Delta 15.6" Dual Monitor 1080P HDR' at $239.99.

findings.label: Measured peak brightness and colour accuracy
findings.value: 372 cd/m² SDR and 578 cd/m² HDR peak; ΔE average 0.74 and max 1.69 in sRGB mode; 100% sRGB, 99% DCI-P3; weight 1.07 kg
findings.source_title: Asus ZenScreen Duo OLED review: Portable OLED perfection (Expert Reviews, Sasha Muller, 2025-06-27)
findings.note: The review does not name its instrument and gives no per-panel split. White point measured 6,098 K, slightly warm. This is the OLED model, not the 14-inch FHD+ IPS ZenScreen Duo that ChatGPT showed at $249.99 (deskgearhq lists the IPS model as MB14FCD).

findings.label: Behaviour on a single laptop cable at high brightness
findings.value: Reviewer says one cable is enough below about 50% brightness; above that, 'the MQ149CD will go into a reboot loop'
findings.source_title: Asus ZenScreen Duo OLED review (Expert Reviews, 2025-06-27)
findings.note: Tested with one USB-C cable from a Dell Pro 14 Premium driving both screens. The spec sheet lists two USB-C inputs with DP Alt Mode and one mini-HDMI input. A 30 W USB-C charger is in the box.

findings.label: Brightness on laptop power (reviewer finding, no figure)
findings.value: Macworld (Simon Jary): 'the Trio's screens can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'; maximum brightness needs a power adapter plugged into one of the Trio's USB-C ports
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review: MacBook QHD dual screen wingspan (Macworld, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro over two USB-C cables. The rated 300 nits is the maker's figure; Macworld measured no nits. Base M1/M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo need Mobile Pixels' driver; Macworld says M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and any M4/M5 MacBook can run it without the software.

findings.product: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender (older model, not the S-series we link)
findings.label: Measured brightness, contrast, sRGB coverage and colour error
findings.value: 177 cd/m² average and 193.1 cd/m² max; contrast 247:1; 79% sRGB; ColorChecker ΔE 4.59 average
findings.source_title: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender review: Clunky and more fragile than standalone portable monitors (Notebookcheck, Allen Ngo, 2022-07-23)
findings.note: Instruments: X-Rite i1Pro 2, Argyll 3D, Calman. Test laptop: HP Pavilion Plus 14, with one USB-C+DP cable per screen. These figures do not carry over to the FOPO S1, S7, S10, S11 or S9G and must not be put in those rows. Use them only as background on the brand, or leave them out.

findings.label: Video path on Mac (reviewer finding)
findings.value: MacBook Air and MacBook Pro need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter ($59 on sale, $99 regular), which uses DisplayLink chips and the free DisplayLink driver; Windows laptops run it through one USB-C cable with DP Alt Mode/Thunderbolt and MST
findings.source_title: Xebec Tri-Screen 3 review (Serious Insights, Daniel W. Rasmus, 2026-05-06)
findings.note: No measured brightness or colour figures; the panels are 'rated up to 300 nits' (maker's figure), two 13.3-inch 1920×1080 IPS at 60 Hz, weight 3.6 lb. Xebec's comparison page, read 2026-11-21, lists the Tri-Screen 3 at $699 (was $778) and the Mac adapter at $59 (was $99).

unsourced: Lab-measured brightness, contrast or colour for the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro: Macworld, CHIP.pl (Kacper Cembrowski, 2026-09-18) and Android.com.pl (Łukasz Pająk, 2026-08-25) each repeat maker specs (300 nits, 100% sRGB, 1000:1, 11 W) and name no instrument. RTINGS covers only the original Trio. I found no Notebookcheck, PCMag or Tom's Hardware review.
Lab-measured brightness for the Xebec Tri-Screen 3: Serious Insights gives only the 300-nit rating, and Xebec's help-center spec is the maker's figure.

Lab-measured brightness for the Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro: Mightygadget, Homecrux and B&H repeat the 350-nit spec. The 250-nit (computer power) vs 300-nit (external power) figures I found are from Mobile Pixels' FAQ for the original Duex Float, not the 2 Pro.
Any named-lab measurement of the FOPO S1, S7, S10, S11, S9G or S788: the only Notebookcheck FOPO review is the older 12-inch triple.
